office_does: The county clerk is the clerk of the superior court: the office files and keeps court records, attends court, enters orders and judgments, and handles the court's money.
race_blurb: An open seat after Clerk Debra Van Pelt retired in May 2026, so the winner takes office at certification and then serves the full four-year term. Former chief deputy clerk Dierdre Butler (Prefers Democratic Party) led the primary with 33.6%; Juvenile Court Services office manager Maria Hazelo (Prefers Republican Party) was second with 26.3% and has Van Pelt's endorsement.

candidates.summary: Coupeville resident who worked in the Island County Clerk's Office from 2014 to 2020, rising from deputy clerk to chief deputy, and has worked in accounts payable in the Auditor's Office since 2020. She ran for clerk in 2022 against Van Pelt.
highlights: Former chief deputy clerk; in the Auditor's Office accounts payable since 2020 [S1][S3]
Promises to modernize operations, streamline record-keeping and reduce delays [S2][S4]
Would borrow processes from other counties and teach the public what the office does [S5]
Says she will carefully manage the clerk's budget on behalf of taxpayers [S3][S4]
Endorsed by the Island County Democratic Party [S8][S9]

experience.basis: Six years inside the Clerk's Office up to chief deputy plus county finance work, but has not held the elected office and is running for an open seat.

spending.basis: Pledges careful budget management and running the office efficiently and responsibly on behalf of taxpayers, with no new spending proposals.

candidates.summary: Oak Harbor resident and Island County Juvenile Court Services office manager, about 20 years with the county, who also serves as the court's liaison to the state Administrative Office of the Courts.
highlights: Manages court-services operations, records, filings, grants, payroll and purchasing [S1]
Promises modernized court records systems, shorter waits and better public access [S1][S2]
Proposes staff training, de-escalation training and a coaching-style approach to retain staff [S5]
Endorsed by the Island County Republican Party and retired Clerk Debra Van Pelt [S8][S4]

experience.basis: About two decades of county court administration, though not in the Clerk's Office, running for an open seat.
